title: Isolate PCSX2 crashes linked to EZFRD64.dll controller drivers
summary: Use a controlled unplug test to verify whether a legacy controller driver is implicated before removing it.
heroAlt: A wireless PlayStation 2 style controller and its USB receiver.

Isolate PCSX2 crashes linked to EZFRD64.dll controller drivers

blocks.text: PCSX2 documents crashes associated with a buggy third-party controller driver known as EZFRD64.dll, commonly located in C:\Windows\USB_Vibration. Its guidance says the driver can corrupt memory in programs it interacts with. Establish that the crash follows the controller or adapter before changing system files. Do not delete files based only on a similarly named DLL in another directory.

Save work and close PCSX2. Unplug the suspected controller and receiver, then launch the emulator without changing settings. Record whether the crash reproduces and note any matching controller package listed under Installed apps or Control Panel. On a managed computer, ask its administrator before modifying a system driver.

items: 1. With the controller unplugged, launch PCSX2 and reproduce the same startup or menu action.
2. Close PCSX2 normally, reconnect only the suspected controller or adapter, and repeat once. Stop if the crash returns.
3. Inspect only the C:\Windows\USB_Vibration directory cited by PCSX2; do not search-delete DLLs across Windows.
4. If the crash correlates with the device, uninstall the matching controller driver package through Installed apps or Control Panel first.
5. If no package is listed, disconnect the controller and create a system restore point before touching the specific documented driver folder.
6. Remove only the identified faulty driver files and reboot if Windows requests it.

blocks.text: The diagnosis is supported if PCSX2 stays open with the device unplugged, crashes while its suspect driver is active, and stays open after the driver is removed. Reconnect once and test. If the crash persists with that driver absent, this test did not establish the cause; save the emulator log and investigate other changes rather than deleting more files.

items: Crash occurs unplugged too: do not remove the driver; inspect the PCSX2 log and recent changes.
The named directory is absent: this workaround may not apply; do not search-delete similarly named files.
The package returns after reboot: check whether a startup utility reinstalls it.
Other USB devices fail: use the restore point or driver rollback and contact the device vendor.

blocks.text: If removal creates a device problem, use the restore point or reinstall the controller maker’s legitimate driver from its official support site. Test PCSX2 with and without the device attached and preserve the crash log so the driver fault can be separated from an emulator issue.
